assumptions: The opportunity is judged at the planning and pre-validation stage; the absence of customers or completed procurement is treated as uncertainty, while the specific contrary evidence in the supplied research is treated as evidence.

No sponsor, appointed controller, prime-contractor relationship, Polish shared-registry mandate, paid discovery engagement, operator commitment, or supplier-selection path exists beyond what is documented in the supplied candidate and research.
The founder company would retain ownership of a reusable technical core but would not own the public mandate, lawful basis, scheme governance, operator coalition, or participant commitments.

Production work would begin only after a customer-funded milestone and documentary proof of customer authority and binding participation, and production-grade legal, security, assurance, incident-response, and on-call obligations would need to be fully priced and substantially delegated.
Some technical reuse across jurisdictions is feasible, but each deployment would still require material legal, identity, integration, assurance, and procurement adaptation.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The redesign correctly recognizes that compulsory coverage and lawful authority, rather than the status API itself, are the decisive control points. Selling a minimized white-label component only to an authorized controller or prime is a disciplined response, but it is principally a risk-gating insight around a known model rather than evidence of an overlooked, founder-controllable commercial opening.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: An authorized national controller or prime would have a real need for identity matching, operator integrations, auditability, appeals, and reliable status checks. However, no such Polish buyer, mandate, procurement, outsourcing decision, budget, or paid discovery is evidenced, and a major operator already supplies its required account-level control internally. Foreign mandated schemes establish need after authorization, not willingness to buy this supplier's module.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Paid discovery, customer-funded implementation milestones, retained core IP, and recurring operations could create capital-efficient revenue and limit speculative downside. The economics are nevertheless almost entirely unquantified: price, prime share, gross margin, sales cost, procurement duration, support intensity, audit and insurance cost, liability, retention, contract frequency, and the path to 5 million PLN of founder net worth are all unknown. A small number of powerful buyers also creates severe pricing and concentration risk.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: The proposed buyer definition is narrow and coherent, but Poland may present only one scheme-level procurement or a few prime-contractor opportunities, against a base of 17 licensed private betting operators. That is narrow without yet being shown economically meaningful for a specialist subcontractor, and the reviewed law supplies no current national shared-registry trigger.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A focused module could become a preferred technical component inside one authorized deployment, but the controller or prime owns the mandate, institutional relationships, procurement position, and participant commitments. Established identity, public-sector, gambling-compliance, or systems-integration suppliers can build or source similar functionality, and the founder has no evidenced access advantage or route to category control.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A jurisdiction-configurable rules engine, adapter library, and assurance toolkit could be reused in other authorized gambling markets and adjacent exclusion workflows. Expansion is plausible but not automatic: every geography resets authority, procurement, legal interpretation, integrations, certifications, and often channel relationships, so a Polish reference would only partially lower entry costs.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Certified integrations, incident history, operational reliability, and accumulated adapters can create switching friction and learning advantages. They are weaker than control of the scheme itself; a prime can internalize the work, retender it, demand IP concessions, or replace the supplier, while non-personal reliability learnings and standard status APIs offer only a modest technical moat.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The minimized yes/no interface, white-label posture, reusable adapters, and explicit separation of governance from technology are sensible. No evidence shows a material advantage in cost, deployment speed, match quality, assurance, uptime, or procurement risk versus an established prime's internal build or existing vendors, so there is not yet a strong reason for a buyer to change supplier behavior.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: International schemes prove technical feasibility and EU policy favors national self-exclusion coverage, while responsible-gambling scrutiny supports the problem's relevance. The key recommendation is longstanding, the reviewed Polish framework still provides operator-level rather than shared controls, and no current Polish legislative, sponsor, or procurement catalyst is evidenced.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Targeting established primes is more credible than assembling operators directly, but the buyer pool is tiny, opaque, relationship-driven, and procurement-heavy. There is no partner, channel, tender access, sponsor introduction, or repeatable acquisition path, and long enterprise or public-sector cycles plus specialist coordination fit the part-time, low-social-energy founder poorly unless a partner truly owns them.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder can plausibly prototype the technical core with data-engineering and AI leverage, and the paid gate prevents an unjustified production build. A live system remains high-stakes infrastructure requiring expert privacy governance, identity resolution, security certification, appeals, near-continuous availability, incident response, insurance, procurement support, and liability allocation; these cannot be replaced by AI and may exceed part-time capacity without funded partners and operators.

main_structural_strength: The v4 structure stops pretending the founder can manufacture public authority: it places the mandate, lawful basis, coalition, and participation commitments with an appointed customer, while milestone funding and retained reusable IP sharply limit speculative capital exposure and align the work with the founder's technical strengths.
primary_score_limiter: The commercial control point remains outside the company. No authorized buyer, Polish scheme trigger, outsourcing decision, paid engagement, operator commitment, or supplier-access channel is evidenced, and any eventual controller or prime would hold both buyer power and the durable institutional moat.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The successful British and Swedish comparators obtain coverage through licence or statutory compulsion, whereas the reviewed Polish law establishes operator-level controls but no shared registry and STS already provides an internal self-exclusion workflow. This directly weakens the premise that a Polish scheme buyer or voluntary demand for an external shared module is imminent.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A materially higher score requires a named authorized sponsor or prime to fund scoped discovery under a credible procurement route, documentary evidence of the mandate and binding operator participation, and buyer-validated proof that the component will be outsourced. It also requires priced implementation and recurring terms showing prime share, assurance and support costs, liability, gross margin, payback, retention, procurement timing, and a credible multi-jurisdiction pipeline.
highest_value_structural_change: Secure an anchor-prime-funded reference deployment under a contract that gives the prime conditional jurisdiction exclusivity only in exchange for minimum paid discovery, implementation, and recurring commitments, while the founder retains the reusable core and rights outside that jurisdiction. This would turn speculative procurement access into funded distribution, protect reuse, and make certification and operations costs recoverable before attempting broader expansion.
